p.WAL-PHASE: The active epic is `campaigns/packages-2026-09/TZ-LIFECYCLE-EXTENSIONS-v0.1.md`; its granular authority for execution state is `campaigns/packages-2026-09/LIFECYCLE-EXTENSIONS-IMPLEMENTATION-LEDGER.md`. R3.4 is integrated, green and mirrored. R7.4's central architecture has passed three claudez audits plus an independent Opus/max adjudication. The disjoint characterization, bounded-read, JTD, typed-output and projection atoms are landed and exactly gated. Pinned transactional state I/O, lease/selected ownership and the read-only tasks adapter are green under the first coherent panel. A9 execution ports, A10 lower projection imports, A11's neutral plan carrier and A12's shared lifecycle application service are now landed through `053b7e37` / `ba874cdf`. The service owns an opaque selected-world bundle, install/resume and phase dispatch behind typed ports; `[llm]`, trace finalisation, presentation and credentials remain physically CLI-owned. A13 trace values precede prompt/run adapters. The owner-approved neutral R7.5 external-work substrate follows R7.4.

facts.WAL-C-FRAMEWORK: Lifecycle is a passive extensible framework, not a coding agent. PDSA is a non-normative external-agent scenario; Plan/Act policy, automatic back-edges and task choice remain outside VibeVM. A reference agent is a future campaign.
facts.WAL-C-EVIDENCE: Verification evidence is valid only for the exact tree/artifact/run identity measured. R7.5 may expose optional read-only requirements/spec-IR facts with stable ids, status, provenance and unmet/stale relations. An external long-running agent may use them to understand remaining requirements and choose its direction; VibeVM exposes facts, not that choice. Absence of that adapter changes no lifecycle.
facts.WAL-C-ALGORITHMIC: VibeVM remains fully useful without an LLM. Paid enhancement is explicit per feature (`off|assist|required`), binds a provider lazily and never replaces the algorithmic baseline.
facts.WAL-C-MECHANISMS: Scheduled extension contributions answer when; sibling qualified mechanisms answer how. Builtins are replaceable providers. R4.0 extracts one pure registry kernel reused by lifecycle, compiler, workspace and later R8 selection; a second collector is forbidden.
facts.WAL-C-DEPLOY: Install materialises the dependency world; package creates portable artifacts; deploy reconciles named destinations through plan/effect/intent/verify/receipt. Clean never silently undeploys. Static skills, Agent Plugins, Cargo applications, client projections, `~/.vibe/bin`, custom installers and future system resources share this plane.

facts.WAL-C-GATES: Development uses exact affected tests. A touched gated Rust crate also runs scoped conform; new or moved source spec edges run specmap in the same atom. Full panel runs only at coherent batch/final boundaries.
facts.WAL-C-WIRE: Every machine wire starts from JTD + registry + corpus + codegen. Never edit `formats/EPOCHS.toml` or generated Rust by hand.
facts.WAL-C-WORKERS: Claudez is the default delegable execution lane while healthy; Opus/max and Sol/native supply judgment or failover. Root owns architecture, review, commits and gates. Accepted worktrees are reclaimed immediately.
facts.WAL-C-PANEL-DENOMINATOR: Current self-check runtime prints `[54/47]` because `STEP_TOTAL` counts lexical call sites while seven calls execute dynamically. Do not use that total as coverage evidence; tooling follow-up is queued in PROP-055.

p.WAL-NEXT: The accepted R7.4 architecture through A12 is landed: state/lease/selected/tasks, three execution ports, the lower projection dependency and a surface-neutral orchestrator application service. Complete A13 trace values, A14 credential-free prompt resolver and A15 hosted `lifecycle_run`, then run the R7.4 boundary panel. Follow with R7.5 exact evidence, optional read-only spec-IR facts and a fake external PDSA orchestrator — no embedded agent policy. Resume R4 registry/transforms after those neutral adapters, per the implementation ledger.
